notes.text:
The friend graph didn't die when the news feed took over Facebook. It just became infrastructure.

That's exactly what's happening to the CRM right now.
notes.source: The Facebook friend graph / news feed analogy used to explain how the CRM is becoming 'just one of many inputs' to an intelligence layer above it.

notes.text:
The typical account executive opens his laptop in the morning and finds waiting for him: a research agent that already read the 10-K, a dialer that coaches him on objections in real time, an orchestration layer that writes call notes back into Salesforce without him touching anything.

None of it, by itself, is earthshaking.

Taken together, you recognize exactly what this is.
notes.source: The 'bottom of the morning' scene describing what a modern AE's AI-assisted workflow looks like.

notes.text:
"All our customer data is in Salesforce" used to be a switching cost.

In five years it won't be. The stickiness is migrating — out of the database, into the reasoning layer that sits above it and treats the database like infrastructure.

Salesforce isn't going away. It's becoming the friend graph.
notes.source: The argument that switching costs shift from data accumulation to orchestration, and that the CRM becomes 'one of many systems of record' the intelligence layer orchestrates across.
